Needs changes before merge. One blocking finding.

The axial span checks keep the reported opposite holes separate. The existing machine and mixed-list refusals pass.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P2] Keep floor detection independent of floor triangulation — `crates/motion/src/drilling/mouth.rs:31`.** The triangle that the ray hits must also have two vertices on the bore rim. A valid floor can have interior vertices. Its ray-hit triangle then fails this condition, although the floor still closes the bore.

   I reproduced this through the built public `recognize` and `recognize_cross` functions. Start with this PR's `opposite_blind_block` fixture. Split each floor triangle at Z = ±17 into three triangles about its centroid. Preserve the winding and the boundary edges. This keeps the same closed solid and hole dimensions.

   The original fixture returns one downward hole and one upward directed hole. The subdivided fixture returns two downward holes and no directed holes. The lower hole has these incorrect values:

   ```text
   entry_z: -17.0
   floor_z: -25.0
   through: true
   ```

   Its actual mouth remains at Z = -25. Its blind floor remains at Z = -17. Detection therefore loses the mouth and direction that this PR must preserve. It also bypasses the directed-hole refusal path. This check does not establish that an unsafe post passes later safety checks.

   Identify the connected floor without requiring the ray-hit triangle itself to contain a rim edge. Keep the protection against unrelated crossing faces. Add a regression with subdivided floors. Check both Z and radial orientations.

Local validation used the trial merge with upstream/main `8f32e8df3a263d6a6f4f0801d1f334373c5a4190`. The merge had no conflicts.

- Motion drilling unit tests: 47 passed.
- Motion `cross_invariance`: 2 passed.
- App `drilling_cross`: 9 passed.
- App `drilling_detect_opposite`: 1 passed.
- App `bore_core`: 5 passed.
- App `drill_undersize`: 3 passed.
- App `golden_cl`: 33 passed.
- App `setup_align_hole_kinds`: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Additional public-library check with subdivided floors: failed as described above. The original fixture passed.

I independently repeated two claimed mutations in temporary copies of the recognition modules. The driver used the PR's block fixture and the built geometry and CL dependencies. Restoring upstream's old `merge_z` failed the Z pin. Restoring upstream's old `merge_found` failed the radial pin. Each restored fix passed again. The worktree source stayed unchanged.

No goldens moved. The PR changes no `.nc` or `.cl` file. No UI file changes need screenshots. No GitHub runner was used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: Keep floor detection independent of floor triangulation.

The detector follows shared edges from the bore rim to the connected floor triangles. The ray-hit triangle needs no rim edge. The end-plane, bore-disc, and finite-segment checks remain.

The regression tests are:
- `subdivided_blind_z_floors_preserve_mouths_and_depths`
- `subdivided_blind_radial_floors_preserve_mouths_and_depths`
- `disconnected_crossing_faces_do_not_close_bore_mouths`

The subdivision tests check two subdivision rounds. They check Z, X, and Y orientations. They preserve the mouths, directions, depths, and blind flags.

Mutation checks passed. Restoring the old detector makes both subdivision tests fail. Restoring the fix makes both pass. Removing the connectivity guard makes the disconnected-face test fail. Restoring the guard makes it pass.

Validation passed:
- All 50 motion drilling tests.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 39 steps, zero failures.
- Motion and app clippy, all targets, with `-D warnings`.
- After formatting only: all seven opposite-hole tests, clippy, and formatting checks.

No goldens changed.

New head: `6f838db102904ce5d9503693f10a24274337f48d`.

Please re-review this head. The PR remains a draft.

Ready for the maintainer to merge. No blocking findings.

This is a safety-tier review. The span checks keep opposite blind holes separate. Detection preserves each mouth and inward direction. The existing generation checks still refuse unsupported work.

The finding from the previous review is resolved. The detector follows shared edges from the bore rim to the floor. The hit triangle needs no rim edge. The tests check two subdivision rounds in Z, X, and Y. A separate test checks that disconnected crossing faces do not close the mouths.

Local validation used the trial merge with upstream/main `4d4a81fcf9c9e39f4dd4b5ac5a2385e4a7a0e0a6`. The merge had no conflicts. All commands ran in the foreground. No GitHub runner was used.

- Motion drilling unit tests: 50 passed.
- Motion `cross_invariance`: 2 passed.
- App `drilling_cross`: 9 passed.
- App `drilling_detect_opposite`: 1 passed.
- App `bore_core`: 5 passed.
- App `drill_undersize`: 3 passed.
- App `golden_cl`: 33 passed.
- App `setup_align_hole_kinds`: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.

I independently repeated three mutations in temporary copies of the recognition modules. The harness used the PR's fixtures and the locally built dependencies. The worktree source stayed unchanged.

1. Restoring upstream's old `merge_z` failed `opposite_blind_z_walls_keep_their_separate_depths`. Restoring the fix passed.
2. Restoring upstream's old `merge_found` failed `opposite_blind_radial_walls_keep_their_separate_depths`. It reported one 50 mm through hole. Restoring the fix passed.
3. Restoring the previous head's floor detector failed both subdivision tests. It reproduced the earlier incorrect lower mouth. Restoring the connected-floor detector passed both tests.

All seven opposite-hole tests also passed together in the temporary harness.

No goldens moved. The PR changes no `.nc` or `.cl` file. It changes no UI file, dependency, build script, or process file. Screenshots are not required.

Not exercised: the original QA project, arbitrary oblique axes, indexed drilling, and a machine run.

Requested before merge: none.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
